messages:
Sam (support): FYI escalation — enterprise customer on Dedicated is getting intermittent 429s despite reserved pool headroom. reported P95 latency spikes too. request id: rId=8a3f2c

Olivia (infra): which pool + pool config? can you paste headers from a failing request?

Sam (support): pool: rp-eu-42, reserved gpus: 8, burst window: default (60s). failing headers from client (redacted):

```
X-Request-Id: rId=8a3f2c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1759001190
X-Reserved-Pool: rp-eu-42
X-Backend-Node: gpu-23
Status: 429
```

Sam (support): customer says they were well under committed throughput on avg. they saw 429s during a short spike (tens of seconds).

Maya (eng-runtime): quick thought — could be smoothing / token-burst algorithm misattributing requests to shared bucket during migration. any routing policy changes around 1759001100-1759001200?

Luis (sre): looking at metrics now — I'm seeing a ~30s spike at 1759001150 where aggregate qps jumped x3 for that pool. smoothing window was 60s so peak exceeded the window and triggered hard-limit enforcement. linking grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/pool/rp-eu-42?from=1759001000&to=1759001300

Sam (support): customer timeline: they had a background job ramping up and then client sent batched requests. they provided a repro curl:

```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\
done; wait
```

Sam (support): they said it only lasted ~25s but client-level retry logic then exacerbated it.

Olivia (infra): thanks. that matches the smoothing behavior — if window < spike duration, tokens get consumed and Remaining goes to 0. two immediate mitigations: 1) increase burst window or burst tokens for rp-eu-42, 2) enable graceful fallback to a lower-tier model for brief overloads.

Maya (eng-runtime): also check kv-cache size on gpu-23; excessive kv eviction can slow token throughput which looks like latency rather than pure QPS cap. can you paste a short log snippet showing backend timings?

Sam (support): paste from customer logs (short):

```
[1759001148] request rId=8a3f2c queue_ms=12 exec_ms=220 token_ms=180 total_ms=412 status=429
[1759001150] request rId=8a3f2d queue_ms=8 exec_ms=120 token_ms=95 total_ms=223 status=200
```

Luis (sre): interesting — one node showing much higher exec/token times. suggests tail latency on that host. I'll run host-level checks for thermal throttling / memory pressure on gpu-23.

infra-bot: [alert] pool rp-eu-42 rate_limit_trigger (count=1) at 1759001151

Sam (support): customer asking for root cause & short-term fix. proposed plan: 1) quick: bump burst tokens for rp-eu-42 by +30% and increase smoothing window to 90s during business hours; 2) medium: add per-client early-fallback config so long bursts can be routed to an alternate variant; 3) long: improve autoscaling pre-warm for scheduled batch jobs.

Olivia (infra): agree with plan. I'll make a config change for the burst window and burst tokens — will apply to rp-eu-42 in the next 2 mins and monitor. patch:

```
# pool rp-eu-42 config diff
burst_window_s: 60 -> 90
burst_token_ratio: 1.0 -> 1.3
```

Olivia (infra): applied. monitor shows X-RateLimit-Remaining staying >0 for similar synthetic spike.

Maya (eng-runtime): I'll queue a runtime task to add a temporary canary fallback rule for that pool: route clients with >100 concurrent short requests to the smaller model.

Luis (sre): checked gpu-23: no OOM, but a noisy neighbor container had high IO; evicted that container and restarted process. post-restart exec_ms dropped ~60%.

Sam (support): told customer we applied burst config and are investigating host-level noise. Customer accepted short-term mitigation but asked for an action item list and reproducible steps.

Maya (eng-runtime): action items for tickets:
- increase smoothing window for rp-eu-42 (done)
- temporary fallback routing (in progress)
- host noise root cause + mitigation (Luis)
- recommend customer implement client-side jitter + exponential backoff and limit concurrency per cluster (Sam)

Sam (support): repro steps we've captured for engineering ticket:
1) run the curl loop above to generate a 20-40s spike
2) observe X-RateLimit-Remaining hits 0 and 429s on pool rp-eu-42
3) remove client retries or add small jitter and concurrency cap to see fewer 429s

Olivia (infra): tagging follow-up: @Maya @Luis please add notes to the ticket and mark high-priority for Dedicated SLA impact.

Maya (eng-runtime): will do. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark: 

Sam (support): closing the customer-facing loop now, will include config diff and recommended client changes in the update. :thumbsup:
